question: A shared project supports a process that changes every quarter. Which practice best keeps the project trustworthy over time?
options: A) Name an owner and a review date so the instructions and the documents are checked each quarter.
B) Re-upload every document once a week so that the knowledge base is refreshed whether or not it changed.
C) Ask anyone who spots an error to correct the knowledge base themselves whenever they happen to notice.
D) Rely on members to say in their prompts which parts of the documents are now out of date.
correct_answers: A) Name an owner and a review date so the instructions and the documents are checked each quarter.
explanations: Correct. Accountability plus a scheduled review is what keeps configuration aligned with a changing process.
Re-uploading unchanged files costs effort without detecting anything that actually changed.
Ad hoc fixes by whoever notices leave gaps and produce inconsistent, unrecorded changes.
This assumes every member already knows what changed, which is rarely true.
